evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.reasoning: Clear reef-monitoring purpose and users identified with need explained. Goals implied but objectives/requirements not quantified. References are bare URLs, lacking specific payload performance detail.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.

criteria.reasoning: Gantt with weekly tasks plus descriptions shows feasible schedule. No robust contingency provision or rationale linking plan to mission, and no explicit planned information-sources list.

evidence.quote: My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.reasoning: Only background reading and tutorials claimed. No results, plots, calculations or STK output shown. Single orbit statement is fundamentally wrong, so no useful technical progress demonstrated.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines.

criteria.reasoning: Logical headings, readable writing, generally consistent formatting. Gantt presented but without caption/number. In-text numbers match URL footnotes, but citations are bare URLs not proper style.

technical_issues.issue: Geostationary orbit at 600 km is incorrect; GEO is ~35786 km, 600 km LEO cannot remain fixed above reef.
Editing & Finalisation text says Weeks 7 and 8 reserved but chart shows Weeks 9-10; due 20/11/20 inconsistent with chart ending 16/11.
60% killed in 2016 plus another 50% perished in 2017 exceeds 100% and misrepresents mortality statistics without clarification.

overall: Good mission idea for Australia with feasible schedule, but lacks quantified requirements, source list, and any real technical results, plus major orbit error.
